Tsun is also a middle author of WAN2015 in Science, which reported that the lysosomal transporter SLC38A9 signals arginine sufficiency to mTORC1. PubMed lists both papers at the Whitehead Institute and the MIT Department of Biology.

highlights.TSU2013: First author: showed that FLCN-FNIP is a GAP for RagC/D, which lets Rag proteins bind and activate mTORC1 at the lysosome.
highlights.WAN2015: Middle author: co-author of the study showing that SLC38A9 signals arginine sufficiency to mTORC1.

Ullern H.lab_name: Department of Molecular Medicine, Institute of Basic Medical Sciences, University of Oslo (Oslo, Norway)
Ullern H.role: First author of a study of p62 build-up in FLCN-deficient Birt-Hogg-Dube kidney cancer cells.
Ullern H.sub: Department of Molecular Medicine, Institute of Basic Medical Sciences, University of Oslo
story: Halvor Ullern was first author of the Atlas study ULL2026 in Autophagy Reports. It used kidney cancer cells from patients with Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome, who lack the FLCN gene. Without FLCN, TFEB stays in the nucleus and mTORC1 is overactive, yet general autophagy and LC3 lipidation are not changed. Even so, the autophagy receptor p62 (SQSTM1) collects in enlarged puncta, and the same was seen in kidney tumours from a Norwegian patient group. So p62 build-up can happen without a general autophagy failure. PubMed lists Ullern at the University of Oslo.

highlights.ULL2026: First author: reported that FLCN loss causes p62 accumulation even though bulk autophagy flux stays normal.

Um SH.lab_name: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research (Basel, Switzerland)
Um SH.role: First author of the 2004 Nature paper on S6K1 deletion, obesity and insulin sensitivity in mice.
Um SH.sub: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research, Basel
story: Sung Hee Um was first author of the Atlas study UMX2004 in Nature. In mice, deleting S6K1, a kinase downstream of mTORC1, protected against obesity that comes with age or a rich diet. The mice also kept better insulin sensitivity. It is a mouse study. PubMed lists Um at the Friedrich Miescher Institute in Basel.

highlights.UMX2004: First author: showed that mice lacking S6K1 resist age- and diet-induced obesity and stay insulin sensitive.

Urfer SR.lab_name: Department of Pathology, University of Washington (Seattle, Washington, USA)
Urfer SR.role: First author of the randomized trial of short-term rapamycin in middle-aged companion dogs.
Urfer SR.sub: Department of Pathology, University of Washington · Dog Aging Project, Seattle
story: Silvan Urfer was first author of the Atlas study URF2017 in GeroScience. It was a randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 24 healthy middle-aged pet dogs. They got low-dose rapamycin or placebo for 10 weeks. The treated dogs had no clinical side effects, and heart ultrasound suggested better heart function. The trial was small and short, so it only supports testing in larger groups. PubMed lists Urfer at the University of Washington and the Dog Aging Project in Seattle.

highlights.URF2017: First author: reported that 10 weeks of low-dose rapamycin caused no clinical side effects in pet dogs and may have improved heart function.

Vellai T.lab_name: Department of Biology, University of Fribourg (Fribourg, Switzerland)
Vellai T.role: First author of the 2003 Nature paper showing that silencing TOR extends lifespan in C. elegans.
Vellai T.sub: Department of Biology, University of Fribourg (affiliation on VEL2003)
story: Tibor Vellai was first author of the Atlas study VEL2003 in Nature. In the roundworm C. elegans, silencing the single TOR gene roughly doubled lifespan. This showed that cutting TOR activity can lengthen life in animals very distant from mammals. It is a worm study. PubMed lists Vellai at the University of Fribourg on this paper.

highlights.VEL2003: First author: showed that silencing TOR roughly doubles lifespan in C. elegans.

Munaretto GM.lab_name: Universidade do Contestado, Campus Concordia (Concordia, Brazil)
Munaretto GM.role: Last author of a meta-analysis of everolimus in heart transplant recipients.
Munaretto GM.sub: Universidade do Contestado, Campus Concordia, Santa Catarina
story: Giancarlo Maruri Munaretto was last author of the Atlas study VITTE2026 in JHLT Open, a meta-analysis of 60 studies with 1786 heart transplant recipients. Everolimus-based treatment slowed cardiac allograft vasculopathy on ultrasound and kept kidney function better when the dose of calcineurin inhibitors was lowered. Death rates were about the same, while side effects and stopping of treatment were more common. PubMed lists Munaretto at the Universidade do Contestado in Santa Catarina, Brazil.

highlights.VITTE2026: Last author: co-author of the meta-analysis of everolimus after heart transplantation.

Vitte SH.lab_name: Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora (Barretos, Brazil)
Vitte SH.role: First author of a meta-analysis of everolimus in heart transplant recipients.
Vitte SH.sub: Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora, Barretos
story: Sofia Helena Vitte was first author of the Atlas study VITTE2026 in JHLT Open. The meta-analysis pooled 60 studies with 1786 heart transplant recipients. Everolimus-based treatment reduced the progression of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (relative risk about 0.57) and kept kidney function better when calcineurin inhibitors were reduced. Overall mortality was unchanged, and adverse events and treatment stops were more common. PubMed lists Vitte at the Hospital de Amor Nossa Senhora in Barretos, Brazil.

highlights.VITTE2026: First author: led the meta-analysis of everolimus in heart transplant recipients.

Wagle N.lab_name: Department of Medical Oncology, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
Wagle N.role: First author of the 2014 report of activating MTOR mutations in an exceptional responder to everolimus.
Wagle N.sub: Department of Medical Oncology, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute · Harvard Medical School
story: Nikhil Wagle was first author of the Atlas study WAG2014 in Cancer Discovery. A patient with advanced cancer had a 14-month complete response in a phase I trial of everolimus and pazopanib. Whole-exome sequencing found two MTOR mutations, and lab tests showed both switch mTOR on. This is one patient, so it gives a hypothesis and does not show a general rule for who responds. PubMed lists Wagle at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School.

highlights.WAG2014: First author: found two activating MTOR mutations in a patient with an exceptional response to everolimus.

Walter T.lab_name: Department of Medical Oncology, Hopital Edouard Herriot (Lyon, France)
Walter T.role: First author of the COMPETE phase 3 trial of 177Lu-edotreotide versus everolimus.
Walter T.sub: Department of Medical Oncology, Hôpital Édouard Herriot, Lyon
story: Thomas Walter was first author of the Atlas study WALTER2026 in The Lancet, the COMPETE trial. It was an open-label phase 3 trial in 309 patients with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, randomized 2:1. Radioligand therapy with 177Lu-edotreotide gave longer progression-free survival than everolimus (23.9 versus 14.1 months) and fewer severe treatment-related adverse events (18% versus 40%). PubMed lists Walter at the Hopital Edouard Herriot in Lyon.

highlights.WALTER2026: First author: reported the COMPETE trial result comparing 177Lu-edotreotide with everolimus.

Wang Q.lab_name: Department of Toxicology and Cancer Biology, College of Medicine, University of Kentucky (Lexington, Kentucky, USA)
Wang Q.role: First author of a study of Pdcd4 binding Rictor to block mTORC2 in lung cancer.
Wang Q.sub: Department of Toxicology and Cancer Biology and Markey Cancer Center, University of Kentucky
story: Qing Wang was first author of the Atlas study WANG2026B in Neoplasia. The work used lung cancer cells and xenografts. The tumour suppressor Pdcd4 binds Rictor through three residues (R105, K108, R110) and breaks up the mTORC2 complex. That lowers PFKFB3, a glycolysis enzyme, and slows glycolysis and growth of non-small cell lung cancer. PubMed lists Wang at the University of Kentucky.

highlights.WANG2026B: First author: showed that Pdcd4 binding to Rictor disrupts mTORC2 and lowers PFKFB3 in lung cancer models.

Piatkevich KD.lab_name: College of Life Sciences, Zhejiang University (Hangzhou, China)
Piatkevich KD.role: Last author of the fluorescent protein ticker tape paper that recorded mTOR activity over time in living cells.
Piatkevich KD.sub: College of Life Sciences, Zhejiang University · School of Life Sciences, Westlake University
story: Kiryl Piatkevich was last author of the Atlas study WANG2026C in Science Advances. The team built a 'ticker tape' from self-assembling protein fibres and several colours of fluorescent protein, so that single living cells keep a record of past gene activity. Versions were made for several pathways, including mTOR. With the mTOR version they saw mTOR activity rise and fall with the cell cycle. PubMed lists Piatkevich at Zhejiang University and Westlake University in Hangzhou.

highlights.WANG2026C: Last author: senior author of the ticker tape tool used to see cell-cycle-dependent oscillations in mTOR activity.

Zhang Xiaoxiao.lab_name: Aier Eye Hospital, Jinan University (Guangzhou, China)
Zhang Xiaoxiao.role: Last author of a study of scleral autophagy in form-deprivation myopia.
Zhang Xiaoxiao.sub: Aier Eye Hospital, Jinan University · Aier Eye Hospital Group
story: Xiaoxiao Zhang was last author of the Atlas study WEN2026 in the FASEB Journal. It used human scleral cells and guinea pigs with experimental myopia. Too much autophagy in the sclera (the white of the eye) seemed to link low-oxygen stress to remodelling of the tissue. Rapamycin under the conjunctiva made myopia worse, 3-MA eased it, and atropine slowed it. AMPK/mTOR/P70S6K signalling was measured, but the paper does not show it is the route that causes the effect. PubMed lists Zhang at Aier Eye Hospital, Jinan University, Guangzhou.

highlights.WEN2026: Last author: senior author of the guinea pig and cell study on scleral autophagy in myopia.

Wu JJ.lab_name: Center for Molecular Medicine, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, National Institutes of Health (Bethesda, Maryland, USA)
Wu JJ.role: First author of the 2013 mouse study of lifespan after genetic reduction of mTOR.
Wu JJ.sub: Center for Molecular Medicine, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH
story: J Julie Wu was first author of the Atlas study WUX2013 in Cell Reports. The mice carried a hypomorphic mTOR gene, so they made only about a quarter of the normal amount of mTOR. These mice lived longer and aged more slowly, but the slowing varied from tissue to tissue. It is a mouse study. PubMed lists Wu at the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute in Bethesda.

highlights.WUX2013: First author: showed that mice with reduced mTOR expression live longer, with tissue-specific slowing of aging.

Xiao T.lab_name: Key Laboratory of Systems Health Science of Zhejiang Province, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (Hangzhou, China)
Xiao T.role: First author of a review of nutrient-sensing pathways in adult stem cells.
Xiao T.sub: School of Life Science, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
story: Tianxiong Xiao was first author of the Atlas study XIA2026 in Seminars in Cell & Developmental Biology. It is a review, not new experiments. It proposes that mTOR, AMPK, sirtuins and insulin/IGF-1 signalling work together to steer adult stem cells between rest, activation and differentiation. With age this network drifts out of balance, which may contribute to stem cell exhaustion. PubMed lists Xiao at the Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study.

highlights.XIA2026: First author: wrote the review on how nutrient-sensing pathways including mTOR control adult stem cells.

Xie J.lab_name: College of Animal Science and Technology, Shandong Agricultural University (Tai'an, Shandong, China)
Xie J.role: First author of a piglet study of glutamine against bisphenol A gut injury with AMPK-mTOR changes.
Xie J.sub: College of Animal Science and Technology, Shandong Agricultural University
story: Jiayuan Xie was first author of the Atlas study XIE2026 in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety. In piglets and pig gut cells, bisphenol A damaged the jejunum (part of the small intestine) and its barrier. Glutamine in the diet eased the damage, along with better mitochondrial function and changes in AMPK-mTOR signalling. The paper suggests a link and does not prove the route. PubMed lists Xie at Shandong Agricultural University.

highlights.XIE2026: First author: reported that glutamine reduced bisphenol A gut injury in piglets alongside AMPK-mTOR changes.

Jiao N.lab_name: College of Animal Science and Technology, Shandong Agricultural University (Tai'an, Shandong, China)
Jiao N.role: Last author of a piglet study of glutamine against bisphenol A gut injury with AMPK-mTOR changes.
Jiao N.sub: College of Animal Science and Technology, Shandong Agricultural University
story: Ning Jiao was last author of the Atlas study XIE2026 in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety. The study in piglets and pig gut cells found that glutamine eased bisphenol A damage to the jejunum. Mitochondrial energy metabolism and the gut barrier recovered, and AMPK-mTOR signalling changed too. The authors call the mechanism possible, not proven. PubMed lists Jiao at Shandong Agricultural University.

highlights.XIE2026: Last author: senior author of the piglet study on glutamine and bisphenol A gut injury.

Xu J.lab_name: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (Wuhan, China)
Xu J.role: First author of a review of mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory disease.
Xu J.sub: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
story: Jingting Xu was first author of the Atlas study XU2026B in Inflammation Research. It is a review of what mTORC2, built around the RICTOR protein, does in immune cells. It covers T cell, B cell, macrophage, dendritic cell and NK cell roles. In tissue inflammation its effects depend on the setting: it worsens osteoarthritis and pancreatitis but dampens pro-inflammatory polarization in colorectal cancer. PubMed lists Xu at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan.

highlights.XU2026B: First author: wrote the review on mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory diseases.

Guo F.lab_name: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (Wuhan, China)
Guo F.role: Last author of a review of mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory disease.
Guo F.sub: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
story: Fengjing Guo was last author of the Atlas study XU2026B in Inflammation Research, a review of mTORC2 and its core protein RICTOR in immune cells. mTORC2 acts through AKT, SGK1 and PKC and shapes T cell, B cell and myeloid cell behaviour. Its role in tissue inflammation depends on context, and dual mTORC1/2 inhibitors such as AZD2014 look promising but have open problems. PubMed lists Guo at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan.

highlights.XU2026B: Last author: senior author of the review on mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory diseases.

Yang HJ.lab_name: Structural Biology Program, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)
Yang HJ.role: Middle author on both Pavletich-group mTOR structure papers in Nature, from 2013 and 2017.
Yang HJ.sub: Structural Biology Program, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (papers from 2013 and 2017)
story: Hyo J Yang is a middle author of two Atlas structure papers in Nature. YAN2013 solved the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase and showed that its active site sits in a recess guarded by the FRB domain, which also explains how FKBP12-rapamycin blocks it.

YAN2017 gave cryo-EM structures of mTORC1 and of RHEB-bound mTORC1, showing how RHEB switches the kinase on and how PRAS40 blocks it. PubMed lists Yang at the Structural Biology Program, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, in both papers.

highlights.YAN2013: Middle author: co-author of the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase.
highlights.YAN2017: Middle author: co-author of the structures of mTORC1 with RHEB and PRAS40.

Li R.lab_name: School of Life Sciences, Central China Normal University (Wuhan, China)
Li R.role: Last author of a mouse study of microplastic and DEHP exposure, mTOR and autism-like behaviour.
Li R.sub: School of Life Sciences, Central China Normal University
story: Rui Li was last author of the Atlas study YANG2026 in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety. Young mice were given polypropylene microplastics and the plasticizer DEHP. They developed autism-like behaviour, and the brain showed mTOR activation with impaired autophagy. Rapamycin restored autophagic flux and eased the behaviour changes. It is a mouse study. PubMed lists Li at Central China Normal University in Wuhan.

highlights.YANG2026: Last author: senior author of the mouse study linking microplastic and DEHP exposure to mTOR-driven autophagy impairment.

Yang G.lab_name: School of Life Sciences, Central China Normal University (Wuhan, China)
Yang G.role: First author of a mouse study of microplastic and DEHP exposure, mTOR and autism-like behaviour.
Yang G.sub: School of Life Sciences, Central China Normal University · School of Public Health, Wuhan University of Science and Technology
story: Ge Yang was first author of the Atlas study YANG2026 in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety. In young mice, exposure to polypropylene microplastics and DEHP led to autism-like behaviour. The brain showed mTOR activation and impaired autophagy, and rapamycin reversed both the autophagy defect and the behaviour changes. No human data were involved. PubMed lists Yang at Central China Normal University and at Wuhan University of Science and Technology.

highlights.YANG2026: First author: reported that microplastic and DEHP exposure activates mTOR and impairs autophagy in young mice.

Yao JC.lab_name: University of Texas M.D. Anderson Cancer Center (Houston, Texas, USA)
Yao JC.role: First author of the RADIANT-3 phase 3 trial of everolimus in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.
Yao JC.sub: University of Texas M.D. Anderson Cancer Center, Houston
story: James C. Yao was first author of the Atlas study YAO2011 in the New England Journal of Medicine, the RADIANT-3 trial. It randomized 410 patients with advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours to everolimus or placebo. Median progression-free survival was 11.0 months with everolimus and 4.6 months with placebo, and side effects were mostly mild. PubMed lists Yao at the M.D. Anderson Cancer Center in Houston.

highlights.YAO2011: First author: reported that everolimus more than doubled progression-free survival in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.

Yin J.lab_name: School of Life Sciences, Tsinghua University (Beijing, China)
Yin J.role: First author of the cryo-EM structure study of the amino-acid transporter SLC36A1 (PAT1).
Yin J.sub: State Key Laboratory of Membrane Biology, School of Life Sciences, Tsinghua University
story: Jian Yin was first author of the Atlas study YIN2026 in Nature Communications. The team solved cryo-EM structures of human PAT1 (SLC36A1) alone and bound to three different substrates. All three sit in a similar spot, which explains why PAT1 accepts so many amino acid-like molecules. This is a structure study. PAT1's links to lysosomal amino acid export and mTORC1 come from earlier work. PubMed lists Yin at Tsinghua University.

highlights.YIN2026: First author: reported the cryo-EM structures of human PAT1 (SLC36A1) with different substrates.

Yu J.lab_name: Department of Anesthesia, Tianjin Medical University General Hospital (Tianjin, China)
Yu J.role: First author of a mouse study of hydrogen gas, mTOR and myelination in sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
Yu J.sub: Department of Anesthesia, Tianjin Medical University General Hospital · Tianjin Institute of Anesthesiology
story: Jiafeng Yu was first author of the Atlas study YU2026 in Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology and Biological Psychiatry. In mice with sepsis-associated encephalopathy, mTOR was overactive in the prefrontal cortex, which held back oligodendrocyte maturation and myelin and led to memory problems. Inhaled hydrogen gas and rapamycin both lowered mTOR activity, restored myelination and improved cognition. It is a mouse study. PubMed lists Yu at Tianjin Medical University General Hospital.

highlights.YU2026: First author: reported that hydrogen gas restrains mTOR overactivation and improves cognition in septic mice.

Yu Yang.lab_name: Department of Anesthesia, Tianjin Medical University General Hospital (Tianjin, China)
Yu Yang.role: Last author of a mouse study of hydrogen gas, mTOR and myelination in sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
Yu Yang.sub: Department of Anesthesia, Tianjin Medical University General Hospital · Tianjin Institute of Anesthesiology
story: Yang Yu was last author of the Atlas study YU2026 in Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology and Biological Psychiatry. The mouse study found that mTOR hyperactivation in the prefrontal cortex impairs oligodendrocyte maturation and causes cognitive deficits after sepsis. Hydrogen gas and rapamycin suppressed mTOR, restored myelination and improved cognition. PubMed lists Yu at Tianjin Medical University General Hospital.

highlights.YU2026: Last author: senior author of the mouse study on hydrogen gas, mTOR and myelination.

Yu L.lab_name: Laboratory of Immunology, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health (Bethesda, Maryland, USA)
Yu L.role: First author of the 2010 Nature paper on mTOR, the end of autophagy and lysosome reformation.
Yu L.sub: Laboratory of Immunology, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, NIH
story: Li Yu was first author of the Atlas study YUX2010 in Nature. Working in rat kidney cells, the paper showed that mTOR is switched off when autophagy starts, then switches back on during long starvation. The renewed mTOR activity ends autophagy and drives autophagic lysosome reformation, where new lysosomes bud off from autolysosomes. The process was also seen in several animal species. PubMed lists Yu at the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in Bethesda.

highlights.YUX2010: First author: showed that reactivated mTOR terminates autophagy and drives lysosome reformation.

Zeng H.lab_name: Department of Immunology, St Jude Children's Research Hospital (Memphis, Tennessee, USA)
Zeng H.role: First author of the 2013 Nature paper on mTORC1 and regulatory T cell function.
Zeng H.sub: Department of Immunology, St Jude Children's Research Hospital
story: Hu Zeng was first author of the Atlas study ZEN2013 in Nature. In mice, regulatory T cells (Treg cells) keep mTORC1 activity higher than other T cells. Deleting raptor, a key mTORC1 part, only in Treg cells destroyed their suppressive function and caused a fatal early inflammatory disease. mTORC1 acted through cholesterol and lipid metabolism, including the mevalonate pathway. PubMed lists Zeng at St Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis.

highlights.ZEN2013: First author: showed that mTORC1 is needed for the suppressive function of regulatory T cells in mice.

Li G.lab_name: College of Life Sciences, Yantai University (Yantai, China)
Li G.role: Last author of a mouse study of pungenin and hair regrowth with PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR gene changes.
Li G.sub: College of Life Sciences, Yantai University
story: Gang Li was last author of the Atlas study ZHAI2026 in Molecules. In mice with hair loss induced by DHT, a plant compound called pungenin applied to the skin sped up hair regrowth and lowered type II 5-alpha-reductase. Gene expression analysis suggested changes in PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR signalling. These are transcript-level changes in a mouse model. PubMed lists Li at Yantai University.

highlights.ZHAI2026: Last author: senior author of the study on pungenin, hair regrowth and PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR gene expression.

Zhai W.lab_name: College of Life Sciences, Yantai University (Yantai, China)
Zhai W.role: First author of a mouse study of pungenin and hair regrowth with PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR gene changes.
Zhai W.sub: College of Life Sciences, Yantai University
story: Wencai Zhai was first author of the Atlas study ZHAI2026 in Molecules. In hair follicle cells and in mice with DHT-induced hair loss, the plant compound pungenin reduced type II 5-alpha-reductase and sped up hair regrowth when applied to the skin. The work points to changes in PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR gene expression. It is a preclinical study. PubMed lists Zhai at Yantai University.

highlights.ZHAI2026: First author: reported that pungenin promotes hair regrowth in mice with changes in PI3K/AKT/FoxO/mTOR signalling.

Zhang Jingyue.lab_name: School of Pharmacy, Lanzhou University (Lanzhou, China)
Zhang Jingyue.role: First author of a study of the Xingxiao Pill in breast cancer models and the ErbB3/PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
story: Jingyue Zhang was first author of the Atlas study ZHANG2026C in the Journal of Ethnopharmacology. The Xingxiao Pill, a traditional Chinese formula, slowed the growth of 4T1 breast cancer cells in culture and in mice. It lowered ErbB3/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling and changed amino acid metabolism. Cinnamic acid and palmitic acid were found to bind mTOR. PubMed lists Zhang at Lanzhou University.

highlights.ZHANG2026C: First author: reported that the Xingxiao Pill inhibits breast cancer growth with lower ErbB3/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling.

Zhou N.lab_name: Department of Oncology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University (Harbin, China)
Zhou N.role: First author of a study of TET1, MRPS17 and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling in lung adenocarcinoma.
Zhou N.sub: Department of Oncology, First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University
story: Nan Zhou was first author of the Atlas study ZHOU2026 in the Journal of Molecular Histology. The enzyme TET1 removes methyl marks from the MRPS17 gene promoter, so MRPS17 is made in larger amounts in lung adenocarcinoma. More MRPS17 turns up PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling and speeds up cell growth, migration and invasion. Knocking MRPS17 down caused cell death and slowed tumours in cells and mice. PubMed lists Zhou at Harbin Medical University.

highlights.ZHOU2026: First author: reported that TET1-driven MRPS17 expression activates PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling in lung adenocarcinoma.

You H.lab_name: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (Wuhan, China)
You H.role: Last author of a mouse and cell study of corilagin in osteoarthritis with PI3K/AKT/mTOR and autophagy changes.
You H.sub: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
story: Hongbo You was last author of the Atlas study ZHOU2026B in International Immunopharmacology. Corilagin, a natural plant compound, eased experimental osteoarthritis in mouse cartilage cells and in a mouse knee-injury model. It blocked PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NF-kB signalling and restored autophagic flux, which cut cartilage damage. PubMed lists You at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan.

highlights.ZHOU2026B: Last author: senior author of the study on corilagin, autophagy and osteoarthritis in mice.

Zhou R.lab_name: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (Wuhan, China)
Zhou R.role: First author of a mouse and cell study of corilagin in osteoarthritis with PI3K/AKT/mTOR and autophagy changes.
Zhou R.sub: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
story: Ruijia Zhou was first author of the Atlas study ZHOU2026B in International Immunopharmacology. In mouse cartilage cells and a mouse osteoarthritis model, corilagin lowered inflammation and cartilage breakdown. It did so by inhibiting PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NF-kB signalling and restoring autophagic flux. PubMed lists Zhou at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan.

highlights.ZHOU2026B: First author: reported that corilagin restores autophagy and protects cartilage in mouse osteoarthritis.

Zinzalla V.role: First author of the 2011 Cell paper on activation of mTORC2 by the ribosome.
story: Vittoria Zinzalla was first author of the Atlas study ZIN2011 in Cell. A genetic screen in yeast, followed by work in mammalian cells, showed that ribosomes, but not protein synthesis itself, are needed for mTORC2 signalling. Active mTORC2 binds the ribosome, and insulin-driven PI3K signalling increases that binding. Findings in melanoma and colon cancer cells suggest it matters in cancer. PubMed lists Zinzalla at the Biozentrum, University of Basel.

highlights.ZIN2011: First author: showed that mTORC2 is activated by association with the ribosome.
